clue.text: Vote cast for act after initial display of talent by male … in this?

definitions.text: Vote cast for act after initial display of talent by male … in this?

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word talent is what is put on show first

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male
X is the mark a voter puts on a ballot paper

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about, so the letters of for act are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer is voted through after showing talent on a TV talent contest, the place where this happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a British TV talent show where viewers vote acts through. 'cast' signals the anagram of 'for act'; 'after' sets the earlier pieces in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British television talent contest in which the public votes on performers.

clue.text: Fool to take on companion that's a jerk

parts.note: a twit is a fool
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An idiot who takes on a partner turns out to be a nasty piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a sudden spasmodic movement, a jerk of a muscle.

clue.text: Volume of wine, formerly

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, often used as communion wine

explanation.surface: Someone recalls how much wine they used to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a Spanish red wine, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is size or amount of space taken up, so volume.

clue.text: Newspaperman tried to free a US criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A journalist attempted to get an American lawbreaker released.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist in charge of the longer articles in a paper is a newspaperman.

clue.text: Youngster engaged by Tory workers to deliver letters

indicators.note: engaged in the sense of held within, so the youngster sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
ants are the classic worker insects
a son is a youngster

explanation.surface: A young lad is hired by Conservative activists to hand out the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliver letters' suggests a postman, but letters here means characters of the alphabet; 'engaged by' signals the youngster held inside the Tory workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonants are a class of the alphabet's characters, all except the vowels.

clue.text: Pop out to meet old friend

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters of pop are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad nips out to meet an old mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a colleague or pal, from 'opposite number'.

clue.text: Where people went for cures in times past

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words times past

explanation.surface: A history note about where the sick used to go for treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Spas are resorts with mineral springs that people visited for health treatments.

clue.text: Tuesday's solution Around end of spring, BEEFE you'll need coat on … S N H E O here in Devon?

indicators.note: around means the phrase for coat on goes round the other piece

parts.note: to paint on is to apply a coat

indicators.note: the last letter of the word spring

explanation.surface: Even at the end of spring you will need a coat in this seaside town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held has stray letters from the previous day's printed grid; the clue itself is 'Around end of spring, you'll need coat on here in Devon?'. 'Around' puts PAINT ON round G. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Paignton is a seaside resort town on the south Devon coast.

clue.text: Favourite son's minor A B N D ordeal?

parts.note: wee means small or minor
a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: A beloved boy faces a small trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held has stray letters from the previous day's printed grid; the clue itself is 'Favourite son's minor ordeal?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The most loved one is the dearest, the favourite.

clue.text: Like grannies going hell for leather?

definitions.text: Like grannies going hell for leather?

parts.words: Like grannies going hell for leather?
parts.note: a granny is a kind of knot, and a phrase meaning very fast is built on the speed unit knots

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very quickly, like going hell for leather; grannies are knots.

clue.text: Progressing, having home tutor

parts.note: in means at home
to tutor is to train

explanation.surface: A pupil is making progress with a private teacher at the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under way, in progress, is said to be in train.

clue.text: Press agent has little time for former soccer player

parts.note: PA is the Press Association, a British news agency
a trice is a very short time, as in 'in a trice'

explanation.surface: A publicist has hardly any time for a retired footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Patrice Evra was a French defender who played for Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrice Evra is a retired footballer, so the first name fits a former soccer player.

clue.text: One might entertain unlawful intention during trial?

definitions.meaning: a magician or illusionist entertains audiences
split as ..., a member of the jury with a swindle in mind

explanation.surface: Someone may harbour criminal plans during a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician performing tricks entertains; read in two parts the word suggests a swindling member of a jury.

clue.text: Group assembled near town to welcome Republican leader once

indicators.note: near means the town abbreviation sits right beside the group
to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
T is the abbreviation for town on maps

explanation.surface: A gathered crowd near a town greets a Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy Brandt was Chancellor of West Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Brandt was the West German chancellor, a former head of government.

clue.text: Dutch lager — less than CI A S EMUS a pint — teetotaller N N D consumed

indicators.note: consumed means taken in, so the teetotaller is swallowed by the drink

parts.note: beer is a general word covering lager
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal or a teetotaller

parts.words: less than CI A S EMUS a pint
parts.note: a half is half a pint, less than a full pint

explanation.surface: A Dutch beer in a smaller measure is drunk by someone who doesn't drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held has stray letters from the previous day's printed grid. 'Dutch' is Cockney slang for wife ('my old Dutch'), not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate British slang for one's wife.

clue.text: Agnes, Tom & I are mixed up in this?

definitions.text: Agnes, Tom & I are mixed up in this?

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters of the names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three people named in the clue are tangled up together in a romantic arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: three people mixed up together is the arrangement the French phrase names.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for a household of three involved together romantically.

clue.text: Islander spotted traffic W problem on main road N to Canada

parts.note: a jam is a traffic hold-up
the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Caribbean visitor is seen in a jam on the highway into Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held has stray letters from the previous day's printed grid. The A1 is the Great North Road, its 1 standing for an I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Caribbean island of Jamaica is an islander.

clue.text: Somerset town's explosive leader?

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: A town's boss is a firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Minehead is a seaside resort on the Somerset coast.

clue.text: A source of vitamin C: people must eat tons for nourishment

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C

indicators.note: must eat means takes in, so tons goes inside the people

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Health advice: citrus fruit and plenty of food for a well-fed population.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeding, or the provision of food, is nourishment.

clue.text: Rolling about in dome

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles around inside a domed building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' means rich, as in 'rolling in it', not turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wealthy, rolling in money, is moneyed.

clue.text: Years and years in filthy accommodation? Somewhat exaggerated

indicators.note: in places the long time inside the dirty dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, notoriously filthy housing
an age is a very long time, years and years

explanation.surface: Someone has lived for ages in a squalid flat; but perhaps they overstate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical in manner, overdone like an actor's performance.

clue.text: Drink — several rounds for him

parts.note: ale is a drink

indicators.note: rounds in the sense of turns about, so the number is read backwards

parts.note: six is taken as a handful, several

explanation.surface: A man is bought drinks for many rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' turns SIX back to XIS; 'him' is defined by a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexis is a man's first name, so it can stand for a particular him.

clue.text: Made an escape without money abroad

parts.note: broke means penniless
out means outside, away, abroad

explanation.surface: A penniless traveller fled the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To break free of a prison is to escape.

clue.text: So-called TV presenter wants end to hostilities, nothing more

parts.note: pax is Latin for peace, the end of fighting
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A broadcaster wants peace and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Paxman, a British TV interviewer, was nicknamed after a brand of stuffing, hence 'So-called'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the British broadcaster Jeremy Paxman.

clue.text: Top of the charts rock band performing near a city in Lombardy

indicators.note: the top is the first letter of the word charts

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A chart-topping rock group plays near an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, famous for violins.

clue.text: Admiring jewellery at a party

parts.note: a do is a party
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone admires a piece of jewellery at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting fondly is a strong kind of admiring.

clue.text: Artist's model seemed uncomfortable, turning round a bit

indicators.note: turning round means the letters are read backwards
a bit of the words seemed uncomfortable gives the letters

explanation.surface: A life model felt awkward and shifted position slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes EDUN from 'seemed uncomfortable', and 'turning round' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A life model often poses unclothed for artists.

clue.text: Fens cloudy? Stormy, causing puzzlement thus?

definitions.text: Fens cloudy? Stormy, causing puzzlement thus?

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters of fens cloudy are churned up

explanation.surface: A weather forecast for the Fens leaves listeners baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying marshland in eastern England; the scrambled letters are themselves a picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bewildered or muddled manner, the way puzzling things are done.
